note.note:
History:
• Chief complaint: Sudden-onset dizziness with spinning sensation (vertigo) beginning ~2 hours ago while preparing breakfast.  
• Course: Constant for past 2 hours; unable to walk straight because room feels as if moving.  
• Associated symptoms: Ear “buzzing” (tinnitus), nausea (no vomiting), feeling shaky.  
• Relevant negatives: No limb weakness, no hearing loss, no ear pain or discharge, no recent viral illness, no fever.  
• Prior episode: Similar vertigo 1 month ago lasting 5–10 min and self-resolved.

Past Medical History:
• Premature ovarian failure – on hormone-replacement therapy (HRT).  
• Medications: HRT (specific agent/dose not documented).  
• Allergies: None reported.  
• No other chronic illnesses or surgeries mentioned.

Physical Examination:
(Conducted via video; limited)  
• General: Appears dizzy, able to ambulate but unsteady.  
• Neurologic: No reported motor weakness of arms/legs; speech intact.  
• ENT: Reports bilateral tinnitus; no ear pain or discharge.  
• Constitutional: Afebrile by history.  
• Mental status: Alert and oriented.

Impression:
• Likely acute labyrinthitis causing vertigo and tinnitus.

Management Plan:
• Prescribed vertigo-relief medication (name not documented), 1 tablet orally three times daily × 10 days; e-prescription sent to Lloyd Pharmacy.  
• Arrange in-person review “within the next few days” for otoscopic exam, blood pressure check, and gait assessment.  
• Safety-net advice: Go to A&E if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or persistent/violent vomiting occur.  
• Patient instructed to contact support to book follow-up appointment.

Patient Summary:
Mary Jane Grey (DOB 1980) developed continuous vertigo with tinnitus and nausea 2 hours ago; exam/history suggest labyrinthitis. She has been given symptomatic medication and will attend an in-person assessment; advised to seek emergency care if red-flag symptoms arise.

Key Takeaways:
• Start prescribed vertigo medication three times daily for up to 10 days.  
• Book and attend face-to-face appointment within a few days for ear and neurological examination.  
• Seek immediate care if weakness, severe headache, or uncontrollable vomiting develops.

Next Steps:
• In-person ENT/neurologic exam with vitals and gait assessment.  
• Consider further investigations (e.g., audiometry, vestibular testing) if symptoms persist or worsen.  
• Review response to medication at follow-up visit.
